subject: English
passage: In their research on workplace flexibility, economists Ibtisam Hijazi and Kayode Alabi examine companies' adoption of the unconventional four-day work week model. This approach generally allows employees to work the same total hours in four days instead of five, giving them a three-day weekend while maintaining full-time status. As the researchers document, that's what happened when Riverside Marketing implemented the model. Only about 15% of employees initially embraced the longer daily schedule, leading to coordination problems and reduced team efficiency. But the researchers also highlight tech startup CloudVision, which saw marked improvements in both productivity and employee satisfaction after many workers adapted quickly to the concentrated schedule. Hence, the four-day work week model may ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: hold greater potential for tech startups than for traditional marketing firms.
choices.B: cause most companies that use the model to reduce the total number of required work hours over time.
choices.C: prove beneficial for some companies but problematic for others.
choices.D: more clearly demonstrate differences in certain companies' management quality than traditional schedules do.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer. In one example, a company experienced problems and reduced efficiency by using the four-day work week model. In the other example, a company saw improvements in productivity and satisfaction. This suggests that some companies may have more success than others using the four-day work week model.
